meta.title: Global Infrastructure Globe — Combined
meta.dedupe_policy: Same facility collapsed within a category. Dual-role places (e.g. airport as busiest + cargo) kept as separate pins.

render_modes.note: Heatmap categories still keep underlying points for focus/details; the globe draws a density field instead of a pin forest.

pins.name: Port of Shanghai (Yangshan)
pins.fact: Shanghai has been the world's busiest container port every year since 2010.

pins.name: Port of Singapore
pins.fact: It connects to over 600 ports in 123 countries, making it the world's leading transshipment hub.

pins.name: Ningbo-Zhoushan Port
pins.fact: It handles the largest amount of total cargo tonnage of any port globally.

pins.name: Port of Shenzhen (Yantian)
pins.fact: It is actually a collective name for several ports spread along Shenzhen's 260 km coastline.

pins.name: Port of Qingdao
pins.fact: Its Qianwan terminal opened one of Asia's first fully automated container terminals in 2017.

pins.name: Port of Guangzhou (Nansha)
pins.fact: Nansha sits where the Pearl River meets the South China Sea and feeds the Greater Bay Area.

pins.name: Port of Busan
pins.fact: It is one of the world's top transshipment hubs and handles most of South Korea's container traffic.

pins.name: Port of Tianjin
pins.fact: It is northern China's largest port and the main sea gateway for Beijing.

pins.name: Jebel Ali Port
pins.fact: Jebel Ali is the largest man-made harbour in the world and the biggest port in the Middle East.

pins.name: Port of Rotterdam
pins.fact: It is Europe's largest port and was the world's busiest until Shanghai overtook it in 2004.

pins.name: Port of Hong Kong
pins.fact: It is one of the few major ports globally that still relies heavily on mid-stream operations.

pins.name: Northern Virginia (Loudoun County, 'Data Center Alley')
pins.fact: It is often claimed that a majority of the world's internet traffic passes through Loudoun County.

pins.name: Dublin Data Center Cluster
pins.fact: Data centers use roughly a fifth of Ireland's electricity, which led to a de facto grid-connection pause around Dublin.

pins.name: Switch 'The Citadel' Campus
pins.fact: The campus is designed at about 7.2 million square feet and runs on 100% renewable energy.

pins.name: Stargate Abilene Campus
pins.fact: It is one of the flagship sites of the Stargate AI-infrastructure project.

pins.name: Meta Hyperion (Richland Parish)
pins.fact: Meta has said the campus could eventually have a footprint comparable to a large part of Manhattan.

pins.name: Amazon Project Rainier (New Carlisle)
pins.fact: Amazon built it to train Anthropic's Claude models on its Trainium2 chips.

pins.name: xAI Colossus (Memphis)
pins.fact: xAI says it stood up the initial supercomputer cluster in just 122 days.

pins.name: Frankfurt Data Center Cluster
pins.fact: Frankfurt is the digital capital of continental Europe, housing DE-CIX, the world's largest internet exchange.

pins.name: Singapore Data Center Cluster
pins.fact: Singapore paused new data center approvals from 2019 to 2022 over power and land constraints.

pins.name: Slough Data Center Cluster
pins.fact: The Slough Trading Estate hosts one of Europe's densest concentrations of data centers.

pins.name: Data Center Alley (Ashburn)
pins.fact: Up to 70% of all global internet traffic passes through Northern Virginia.

pins.name: Inner Mongolia Information Park
pins.fact: It is considered one of the largest data center campuses in the world by square footage.

pins.name: CWL1 Campus (Vantage)
pins.fact: Formerly Next Generation Data, it is Europe's largest hyperscale data center facility.

pins.name: Utah Data Center (NSA)
pins.fact: Built by the NSA, it reportedly has a storage capacity measured in zettabytes.

pins.name: QTS Atlanta Metro
pins.fact: It was converted from a massive former Sears, Roebuck & Co. distribution center.

pins.name: Lefdal Mine Datacenter
pins.fact: It is built entirely within a massive abandoned underground olivine mine.

pins.name: Cape Canaveral Space Force Station
pins.fact: It has been the primary launch site for American uncrewed space and military flights since 1950.

pins.name: Baikonur Cosmodrome
pins.fact: Sputnik 1 in 1957 and Yuri Gagarin's Vostok 1 in 1961 both launched from here.

pins.name: Plesetsk Cosmodrome
pins.fact: The Soviet Union denied the site existed until 1983, despite it being one of the world's busiest launch sites.

pins.name: Vandenberg Space Force Base
pins.fact: Its coastal location lets polar-orbit rockets fly south over open ocean rather than populated areas.

pins.name: Guiana Space Centre (Kourou)
pins.fact: Sitting about 5 degrees north of the equator gives rockets extra speed from Earth's rotation.

pins.name: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center
pins.fact: China's first crewed spaceflight, Shenzhou 5 with Yang Liwei, launched from here in 2003.

pins.name: Xichang Satellite Launch Center
pins.fact: It launches many of China's BeiDou navigation satellites from a mountain valley in Sichuan.

pins.name: Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center
pins.fact: It specializes in polar-orbit launches for weather and Earth-observation satellites.

pins.name: Satish Dhawan Space Centre (Sriharikota)
pins.fact: India's Chandrayaan-3 lunar lander launched from here in 2023.

pins.name: Wenchang Space Launch Site
pins.fact: China's coastal Hainan spaceport launched the Tianwen-1 Mars mission in 2020.

pins.name: Kennedy Space Center
pins.fact: Every NASA human spaceflight since 1968 has departed from here.

pins.name: Tanegashima Space Center
pins.fact: Often called the most beautiful rocket launch site in the world due to its coastal cliff location.

pins.name: Starbase (SpaceX)
pins.fact: It was built entirely from scratch by SpaceX exclusively for the Starship program.

pins.name: Narendra Modi Stadium
pins.fact: It is the largest stadium in the world by seating capacity, primarily hosting cricket matches.

pins.name: Rungrado 1st of May Stadium
pins.fact: Its roof is designed to resemble a magnolia blossom and it hosts the Arirang Mass Games.

pins.name: Michigan Stadium
pins.fact: Nicknamed 'The Big House', it is the largest stadium in the Western Hemisphere.

pins.name: Beaver Stadium
pins.fact: Penn State's famous 'White Out' games turn the entire crowd into a sea of white.

pins.name: Ohio Stadium
pins.fact: Known as 'The Horseshoe', it is the home of Ohio State's 'Script Ohio' marching band tradition.

pins.name: Kyle Field
pins.fact: Texas A&M's 'Twelfth Man' tradition has fans standing for the entire game.

pins.name: Tiger Stadium (LSU)
pins.fact: Crowd noise during a 1988 LSU game actually registered as a minor earthquake on a local seismograph.

pins.name: Spotify Camp Nou
pins.fact: It has been the home of FC Barcelona since 1957 and is Europe's largest association football stadium.

pins.name: Melbourne Cricket Ground
pins.fact: It is the largest stadium in the Southern Hemisphere and hosted the 1956 Olympic Games.

pins.name: AT&T Stadium
pins.fact: The Dallas Cowboys' home hangs one of the world's largest high-definition video boards above the field.

pins.name: Neyland Stadium
pins.fact: It is one of the few college stadiums easily accessible by boat via the nearby Tennessee River.

pins.name: Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Plant
pins.fact: It is the largest nuclear power plant in the world by net electrical power rating, though largely offline since Fukushima.

pins.name: Bruce Nuclear Generating Station
pins.fact: It is often called the largest operating nuclear power plant in the world.

pins.name: Kori / Shin Kori Nuclear Complex
pins.fact: It sits near Busan in one of the densest clusters of reactors on Earth.

pins.name: Hanul Nuclear Power Plant
pins.fact: It is South Korea's largest nuclear plant and one of the highest-producing globally.

pins.name: Hanbit Nuclear Power Plant
pins.fact: Formerly known as Yeonggwang, it was renamed in 2013 following requests from local fishermen.

pins.name: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant
pins.fact: It is the largest nuclear plant in Europe and has been heavily contested during the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

pins.name: Gravelines Nuclear Power Station
pins.fact: It cools its reactors using water from the North Sea and also supplies waste heat to a local aquaculture farm.

pins.name: Paluel Nuclear Power Plant
pins.fact: Built on the Normandy coast, it uses seawater from the English Channel for cooling.

pins.name: Cattenom Nuclear Power Plant
pins.fact: Its four cooling towers rise on the Moselle River close to the borders with Luxembourg and Germany.

pins.name: Palo Verde Nuclear Generating Station
pins.fact: It is the largest US nuclear plant and the only one not built beside a large body of water, using treated wastewater for cooling.

pins.name: Jamnagar Refinery Complex
pins.fact: Reliance's Jamnagar site is the largest oil refining complex in the world.

pins.name: Paraguana Refining Center
pins.fact: It combines the Amuay and Cardon refineries on Venezuela's Paraguana Peninsula.

pins.name: Ruwais Refinery
pins.fact: ADNOC's Ruwais complex is the heart of Abu Dhabi's refining and petrochemical industry.

pins.name: SK Ulsan Refinery
pins.fact: It is operated by SK Energy and is the largest single-site refinery in South Korea.

pins.name: GS Caltex Yeosu Refinery
pins.fact: It is run by GS Caltex, a joint venture between Korea's GS Group and Chevron.

pins.name: Motiva Port Arthur Refinery
pins.fact: Operated by Motiva Enterprises, it is the largest oil refinery in the United States.

pins.name: Marathon Galveston Bay Refinery
pins.fact: The Texas City site was the location of the deadly 2005 explosion at the former BP refinery.

pins.name: Al-Zour Refinery
pins.fact: It is Kuwait's newest mega-refinery and one of the largest in the Middle East.

pins.name: Marathon Garyville Refinery
pins.fact: It is the largest refinery in Louisiana, sitting along the Mississippi River.

pins.name: ExxonMobil Baytown Refinery
pins.fact: The refinery is part of an integrated complex that also includes major chemical plants.

pins.name: Burj Khalifa
pins.fact: It is so tall that you can watch the sunset from the ground, take the elevator to the top, and watch it set again.

pins.name: Merdeka 118
pins.fact: Completed in Malaysia, it uses its massive spire to claim the title of the world's second-tallest building.

pins.name: Shanghai Tower
pins.fact: Its twisted 120-degree aerodynamic shape reduces wind loads on the building by 24%.

pins.name: Abraj Al-Bait Clock Tower
pins.fact: Its clock face is the largest in the world and can be seen from kilometers away in Mecca.

pins.name: Ping An Finance Center
pins.fact: It was originally designed to have a 60-meter spire, but it was dropped due to flight path concerns.

pins.name: Lotte World Tower
pins.fact: It is the tallest building in South Korea, with 123 floors.

pins.name: One World Trade Center
pins.fact: Its height of 1,776 feet is a deliberate reference to the year the US Declaration of Independence was signed.

pins.name: Guangzhou CTF Finance Centre
pins.fact: Its elevators travel at about 21 meters per second, among the fastest in the world.

pins.name: Tianjin CTF Finance Centre
pins.fact: It is uniquely designed with a curving glass skin that efficiently channels wind forces.

pins.name: CITIC Tower (China Zun)
pins.fact: Beijing's tallest building takes its shape from the ancient Chinese 'zun' wine vessel.

pins.name: Boeing Everett Factory
pins.fact: It holds the record for the largest building in the world by volume, built originally to assemble the 747.

pins.name: Tesla Giga Texas
pins.fact: It is the second-largest building in the world by volume and produces the Cybertruck.

pins.name: Foxconn Longhua Science Park
pins.fact: Also known as 'Foxconn City,' it functions like a self-contained metropolis with up to 300,000 workers.

pins.name: Volkswagen Wolfsburg Plant
pins.fact: The plant has its own power station and sits beside the Autostadt visitor park.

pins.name: Hyundai Ulsan Plant
pins.fact: It is often cited as the largest single automobile factory in the world.

pins.name: Toyota Georgetown Plant
pins.fact: It is Toyota's largest manufacturing plant outside Japan.

pins.name: Tesla Fremont Factory
pins.fact: Formerly the NUMMI plant operated jointly by GM and Toyota, it now produces multiple Tesla models.

pins.name: Tesla Gigafactory Nevada
pins.fact: It makes batteries and drive units in partnership with Panasonic near Reno.

pins.name: BMW Plant Spartanburg
pins.fact: It is BMW's largest production plant in the world by volume.

pins.name: Tesla Giga Berlin-Brandenburg
pins.fact: It is Tesla's first major vehicle factory in Europe, built in a forested area near Berlin.

pins.name: NASA Michoud Assembly Facility
pins.fact: It is where the colossal core stages of the Space Launch System (SLS) are built.

pins.name: Jean-Luc Lagardère Plant (Airbus)
pins.fact: It was custom-built in France specifically to assemble the massive double-decker A380 airliner.

pins.name: Mitsubishi Motors Mizushima Plant
pins.fact: It is one of Japan's most comprehensive car factories, integrating stamping through final assembly.

pins.name: Rivian Normal Plant
pins.fact: Originally built by Mitsubishi, it was heavily modernized to produce electric trucks and Amazon delivery vans.

pins.name: Marea (Virginia Beach Landing)
pins.fact: Funded heavily by Microsoft and Meta, it is one of the highest-capacity transatlantic cables.

pins.name: Grace Hopper (Bude Landing)
pins.fact: Named after the pioneering computer scientist, it directly connects the US, UK, and Spain.

pins.name: Marea (Sopelana Landing)
pins.fact: It stretches 6,600 kilometers from Virginia to this small coastal town in Spain.

pins.name: Dunant (Saint-Hilaire-de-Riez Landing)
pins.fact: It was the first subsea cable to feature a groundbreaking 12-fiber pair space-division multiplexing design.

pins.name: Marseille Cable Hub
pins.fact: Marseille is a major hub linking Europe to Africa, the Middle East and Asia through submarine cables.

pins.name: Singapore Cable Landing
pins.fact: It is one of the most connected cable landing locations in Asia.

pins.name: Chikura Cable Landing (Japan)
pins.fact: The station in Chiba is a key landing for trans-Pacific cables, including FASTER.

pins.name: Fortaleza Cable Landing (Brazil)
pins.fact: EllaLink connects Brazil directly to Portugal without routing traffic through the United States.

pins.name: Mumbai Cable Landing
pins.fact: Mumbai is India's primary gateway for international submarine cables.

pins.name: Melkbosstrand Cable Landing (Cape Town)
pins.fact: It is South Africa's Atlantic cable station, hosting Equiano and the older SAT-3 cable.

pins.name: SEA-ME-WE 3 (Perth Landing)
pins.fact: At 39,000 kilometers, it is the longest telecommunications cable in the world.

pins.name: FASTER (Bandon Landing)
pins.fact: Backed by Google, it runs straight across the Pacific Ocean from Oregon to Japan.

pins.name: Amitié (Le Porge Landing)
pins.fact: It is currently the highest-capacity transatlantic submarine communications cable ever built.

pins.name: 2Africa (Genoa Landing)
pins.fact: Once complete, it will be the most comprehensive subsea cable serving the African continent.

pins.name: Talatan Solar Park (Gonghe)
pins.fact: Located in the Rajasthan desert, it is the largest solar park in the world by capacity.

pins.name: Golmud Solar Park
pins.fact: Spread across 13,000 acres in Karnataka, India, it was developed entirely on leased farmland.

pins.name: Bhadla Solar Park
pins.fact: It spreads across the Thar Desert, where summer temperatures can exceed 45°C.

pins.name: Pavagada Solar Park
pins.fact: Also known as Shakti Sthala, it was built on farmland leased from thousands of local farmers.

pins.name: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park
pins.fact: It aims to reach 5,000 MW by 2030, which would make it the undisputed largest globally.

pins.name: Benban Solar Park
pins.fact: It is Africa's largest solar complex and sits in the desert near Aswan.

pins.name: Tengger Desert Solar Park
pins.fact: Nicknamed the 'Great Wall of Solar,' it covers 43 square kilometers of an arid Chinese desert.

pins.name: Noor Abu Dhabi (Sweihan)
pins.fact: It features over 3.2 million solar panels and is one of the world's largest single-site solar projects.

pins.name: Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park
pins.fact: Located in Andhra Pradesh, India, it was constructed in an incredibly short span of two years.

pins.name: Longyangxia Dam Solar Park
pins.fact: It sits beside a hydropower reservoir so that hydro and solar generation can complement each other.

pins.name: Huanghe Hydropower Hainan Solar Park
pins.fact: Built in China, it features an accompanying energy storage system to manage grid stability.

pins.name: Datong Solar Power Top Runner Base
pins.fact: It famously includes a section arranged in the shape of two giant pandas when viewed from above.

pins.name: Copper Mountain Solar Facility
pins.fact: Located in Nevada, it is one of the largest photovoltaic solar power plants in the US.

pins.name: Gansu Wind Farm (Jiuquan Wind Power Base)
pins.fact: It is the largest wind farm in the world, consisting of thousands of turbines across the Gobi Desert.

pins.name: Dogger Bank Wind Farm
pins.fact: It is set to become the world's largest offshore wind farm when all phases are complete.

pins.name: Hornsea 2
pins.fact: Located in the North Sea, it is currently the world's largest fully operational offshore wind farm.

pins.name: Muppandal Wind Farm
pins.fact: It is one of India's largest wind clusters, near the southern tip of the country at Kanyakumari.

pins.name: Alta Wind Energy Center
pins.fact: It is among the largest onshore wind farms in the United States, in California's Tehachapi Pass.

pins.name: Jaisalmer Wind Park
pins.fact: It is one of India's biggest onshore wind farms, set in the Thar Desert.

pins.name: Shepherds Flat Wind Farm
pins.fact: It sits on the windy hills south of the Columbia River in Oregon.

pins.name: Roscoe Wind Farm
pins.fact: Its 627 turbines made it the largest onshore wind farm in the world when completed in 2009.

pins.name: Horse Hollow Wind Energy Center
pins.fact: It was the largest wind farm in the world when it was completed in 2006.

pins.name: Walney Extension
pins.fact: Located off the coast of Cumbria, UK, its turbines are among the tallest ever installed.

pins.name: Hornsea Project One
pins.fact: It was the first offshore wind farm globally to exceed 1 gigawatt in capacity.

pins.name: London Array
pins.fact: Situated in the Thames Estuary, it powers nearly half a million UK homes annually.

pins.name: Hong Kong International Airport (HKG)
pins.fact: It is consistently the busiest cargo airport in the world due to its strategic position in Asia.

pins.name: Memphis International Airport (MEM)
pins.fact: It is FedEx's global hub, where most packages are sorted overnight.

pins.name: Shanghai Pudong International Airport (PVG)
pins.fact: It handles the vast majority of international air freight entering and leaving China.

pins.name: Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport (ANC)
pins.fact: Anchorage is often described as within about nine and a half hours' flight of most of the industrialized world.

pins.name: Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport (SDF)
pins.fact: It is home to UPS Worldport, one of the world's largest automated package-handling facilities.

pins.name: Incheon International Airport (ICN)
pins.fact: It acts as the primary gateway for semiconductors and electronics exported from South Korea.

pins.name: Hamad International Airport (DOH)
pins.fact: It is the home hub of Qatar Airways Cargo, one of the world's largest air freight carriers.

pins.name: Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport (TPE)
pins.fact: A large share of its freight is made up of semiconductors and electronics.

pins.name: Miami International Airport (MIA)
pins.fact: It is the top US airport for international freight, with strong flows to Latin America.

pins.name: Dubai International Airport (DXB)
pins.fact: It is the primary hub for Emirates SkyCargo, linking Asia, Europe and Africa.

pins.name: Los Angeles International Airport (LAX Cargo)
pins.fact: It is a crucial trans-Pacific cargo node connecting American consumer markets to Asian manufacturing.

pins.name: Tokyo Narita International Airport (NRT Cargo)
pins.fact: Narita handles more than half of Japan's total international air freight.

pins.name: Three Gorges Dam
pins.fact: It is the world's largest power station and holds so much water it minutely slows the Earth's rotation.

pins.name: Baihetan Dam
pins.fact: It houses sixteen 1,000 MW turbine units, the largest hydro units in the world.

pins.name: Itaipu Dam
pins.fact: Shared by Brazil and Paraguay, it supplies the large majority of Paraguay's electricity.

pins.name: Xiluodu Dam
pins.fact: It is a double-curvature arch dam on the Jinsha River in China, known for highly complex seismic engineering.

pins.name: Belo Monte Dam
pins.fact: It is one of the world's largest and most controversial dams, built on the Xingu River in the Amazon.

pins.name: Guri Dam (Simon Bolivar)
pins.fact: It has historically supplied a large share of Venezuela's electricity.

pins.name: Wudongde Dam
pins.fact: It is one of the thinnest ultra-high arch dams in the world relative to its height.

pins.name: Tucurui Dam
pins.fact: It is the largest hydroelectric plant built entirely with Brazilian technology.

pins.name: Grand Coulee Dam
pins.fact: It is the largest power-producing facility in the United States and the largest concrete structure in the country.

pins.name: Xiangjiaba Dam
pins.fact: It features the massive Shiplift, the largest elevator of its kind in the world for river traffic.

pins.name: Sayano-Shushenskaya Dam
pins.fact: It is Russia's largest power plant and tragically suffered a catastrophic turbine failure in 2009.

pins.name: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL)
pins.fact: Due to its geographic placement, it serves as a two-hour flight hub for 80% of the U.S. population.

pins.name: Dubai International Airport (DXB)
pins.fact: It is the world's busiest airport for international passengers.

pins.name: Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW)
pins.fact: Its land area is larger than the island of Manhattan.

pins.name: London Heathrow Airport (LHR)
pins.fact: It handles all this traffic with just two runways running close to capacity.

pins.name: Tokyo Haneda Airport (HND)
pins.fact: Consistently ranked among the cleanest and most punctual large airports globally.

pins.name: Denver International Airport (DEN)
pins.fact: Its iconic tent-like roof mimics the snow-capped Rocky Mountains, and it is the largest airport in North America by area.

pins.name: Istanbul Airport (IST)
pins.fact: Built entirely from scratch near the Black Sea, it officially opened in 2018 to replace Ataturk Airport.

pins.name: Los Angeles International Airport (LAX)
pins.fact: Its 1961 Theme Building is one of the most recognizable airport landmarks in the world.

pins.name: Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD)
pins.fact: It is named after Butch O'Hare, a US Navy pilot and Medal of Honor recipient from World War II.

pins.name: Indira Gandhi International Airport (DEL)
pins.fact: It is India's busiest aviation hub and features an entirely carbon-neutral terminal.

pins.name: Area 51 (Groom Lake)
pins.fact: Historically unacknowledged by the CIA until 2013, it was the testing ground for the U-2 and SR-71 spy planes.

pins.name: Diego Garcia
pins.fact: This remote Indian Ocean atoll hosts a strategic joint UK-US military base.

pins.name: Fort Bragg
pins.visual_stat: ~160 sq mi; Nickname: 'Home of the Airborne'
pins.fact: It is a major home of US Army airborne and special operations forces.

pins.name: Naval Station Norfolk
pins.visual_stat: Largest naval station in the world (~75 ships)
pins.fact: It hosts dozens of ships and well over a hundred aircraft.

pins.name: Cheyenne Mountain Complex
pins.visual_stat: Nickname: 'The Mountain'; ~2,000 ft of granite overhead
pins.fact: It was built inside a mountain to survive a nuclear attack and supports NORAD operations.

pins.name: Joint Defence Facility Pine Gap
pins.fact: The satellite ground station near Alice Springs is run jointly by Australia and the United States.

pins.name: Camp Bondsteel
pins.fact: Built in 1999 in Kosovo, it is named after a Vietnam War Medal of Honor recipient.

pins.name: Ramstein Air Base
pins.fact: It is the headquarters of US Air Forces in Europe.

pins.name: Kadena Air Base
pins.fact: It is a key Russian strategic bomber base located dramatically high above the Arctic Circle.

pins.name: Camp Humphreys
pins.fact: Its expansion cost roughly 10 billion dollars, making it one of the most expensive overseas US military projects.

pins.name: Thule Air Base
pins.fact: Located in Greenland, it houses a ballistic missile early warning radar capable of surviving extreme Arctic winters.

pins.name: Fort Cavazos (formerly Fort Hood)
pins.fact: It is one of the largest armored military installations in the world, practically functioning as a small city.

pins.name: Kwajalein Atoll (Ronald Reagan Ballistic Missile Test Site)
pins.fact: It serves as a massive target practice zone for unarmed ICBMs launched from California.

pins.name: Yulin Naval Base
pins.fact: Located on Hainan Island, China, it features extensive underground submarine caves carved directly into mountains.

pins.name: TSMC Fab 18 (Tainan)
pins.fact: TSMC's Fab 18 complex is a core site for leading-edge Apple and AI GPU wafers.

pins.name: TSMC Arizona Fab 21
pins.fact: TSMC's first high-volume advanced fab in the United States, outside Phoenix.

pins.name: Samsung Hwaseong Campus
pins.fact: One of Samsung's largest memory and logic manufacturing campuses in South Korea.

pins.name: Intel Fab 42 (Arizona)
pins.fact: Intel's large Ocotillo-site fab built for advanced process technology.

pins.name: Intel Fab 34 (Ireland)
pins.fact: Leixlip is Intel's primary advanced manufacturing base in Europe.

pins.name: SMIC Shanghai
pins.fact: SMIC is China's largest pure-play foundry by capacity.

pins.name: GlobalFoundries Fab 8 (Malta, NY)
pins.fact: A major US specialty/RF and feature-rich process fab in New York's Tech Valley.

pins.name: UMC Fab 12A (Tainan)
pins.fact: UMC's 300mm complex serving automotive and consumer chips.

pins.name: Micron Hiroshima
pins.fact: A key Micron DRAM manufacturing site in Japan.

pins.name: SK hynix Icheon
pins.fact: SK hynix Icheon is central to high-bandwidth memory used in AI accelerators.

pins.name: CATL Yibin Plant
pins.fact: One of CATL's flagship gigafactory clusters in Sichuan, China.

pins.name: CATL Thuringia (Arnstadt)
pins.fact: CATL's first large European cell plant, supplying German automakers.

pins.name: LG Energy Solution Michigan
pins.fact: Major Ultium cell joint-venture capacity for GM EVs in the US Midwest.

pins.name: Panasonic Energy Kansas
pins.fact: Panasonic's US plant supporting Tesla's 4680 cell ramp.

pins.name: Tesla Gigafactory Nevada (Battery)
pins.fact: Tesla's original Nevada gigafactory still anchors pack and cell output.

pins.name: Samsung SDI Seremban
pins.fact: Samsung SDI's large Malaysian plant for automotive battery cells.

pins.name: BYD Blade Battery Plant (Chongqing)
pins.fact: BYD's Blade LFP chemistry underpins its vertically integrated EV stack.

pins.name: Northvolt Ett (Skellefteå)
pins.fact: Sweden's Northvolt Ett was built as Europe's flagship green battery plant.

pins.name: Panasonic Suminoe (Osaka)
pins.fact: Historic Panasonic battery manufacturing base in Osaka.

pins.name: LG Energy Solution Wrocław
pins.fact: LG's Polish plant is one of Europe's largest EV battery cell factories.

pins.name: Ras Laffan Industrial City
pins.fact: Ras Laffan is the heart of Qatar's LNG export machine.

pins.name: Sabine Pass LNG (Cheniere)
pins.fact: Cheniere's Sabine Pass opened large-scale US LNG exports to the world.

pins.name: Freeport LNG
pins.fact: One of the largest US Gulf Coast LNG export terminals.

pins.name: Cameron LNG
pins.fact: A major US LNG export facility on the Calcasieu Ship Channel.

pins.name: Yamal LNG (Sabetta)
pins.fact: Yamal LNG ships Arctic gas via ice-class tankers from Sabetta.

pins.name: Gorgon LNG (Barrow Island)
pins.fact: Chevron's Gorgon is one of Australia's largest LNG projects.

pins.name: Wheatstone LNG
pins.fact: Wheatstone exports LNG from Western Australia's Pilbara coast.

pins.name: Nigeria LNG (Bonny Island)
pins.fact: NLNG on Bonny Island is Africa's landmark LNG export complex.

pins.name: Cove Point LNG
pins.fact: Cove Point is a rare East Coast US LNG export terminal.

pins.name: Calcasieu Pass LNG
pins.fact: Venture Global's Calcasieu Pass uses a mid-scale modular export design.

pins.name: New York Stock Exchange
pins.fact: The NYSE is the world's largest stock exchange by listed market capitalization.

pins.name: NASDAQ MarketSite
pins.fact: NASDAQ lists many of the world's largest technology companies.

pins.name: Shanghai Stock Exchange
pins.fact: SSE is a primary venue for China's largest state and private firms.

pins.name: Japan Exchange Group (Tokyo)
pins.fact: JPX/TSE anchors equity trading for Japan Inc.

pins.name: Euronext Amsterdam
pins.fact: Euronext Amsterdam links historic Dutch markets to modern EU listings.

pins.name: London Stock Exchange
pins.fact: LSE remains a major cross-border listing and trading venue.

pins.name: Hong Kong Exchanges (HKEX)
pins.fact: HKEX is the classic offshore gateway for China capital markets.

pins.name: National Stock Exchange of India
pins.fact: NSE is India's largest exchange by equity trading volume.

points.name: Talatan Solar Park (Gonghe)
points.fact: Located in the Rajasthan desert, it is the largest solar park in the world by capacity.

points.name: Golmud Solar Park
points.fact: Spread across 13,000 acres in Karnataka, India, it was developed entirely on leased farmland.

points.name: Bhadla Solar Park
points.fact: It spreads across the Thar Desert, where summer temperatures can exceed 45°C.

points.name: Pavagada Solar Park
points.fact: Also known as Shakti Sthala, it was built on farmland leased from thousands of local farmers.

points.name: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park
points.fact: It aims to reach 5,000 MW by 2030, which would make it the undisputed largest globally.

points.name: Benban Solar Park
points.fact: It is Africa's largest solar complex and sits in the desert near Aswan.

points.name: Tengger Desert Solar Park
points.fact: Nicknamed the 'Great Wall of Solar,' it covers 43 square kilometers of an arid Chinese desert.

points.name: Noor Abu Dhabi (Sweihan)
points.fact: It features over 3.2 million solar panels and is one of the world's largest single-site solar projects.

points.name: Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park
points.fact: Located in Andhra Pradesh, India, it was constructed in an incredibly short span of two years.

points.name: Longyangxia Dam Solar Park
points.fact: It sits beside a hydropower reservoir so that hydro and solar generation can complement each other.

points.name: Huanghe Hydropower Hainan Solar Park
points.fact: Built in China, it features an accompanying energy storage system to manage grid stability.

points.name: Datong Solar Power Top Runner Base
points.fact: It famously includes a section arranged in the shape of two giant pandas when viewed from above.

points.name: Copper Mountain Solar Facility
points.fact: Located in Nevada, it is one of the largest photovoltaic solar power plants in the US.
